source.method: Visual review of the locked V40 printed steps 6 and 7 panels (chassis shown upside down), rendered privately; no source pixels are copied into authored output
source.observation: The battery lies lengthwise on the loop-tape patch under the deck, between the slotted flange tabs, its wire end toward the rear, pressed up against the deck underside (red arrow up).

placement.orientation: Long axis along the car (installed X); wire end toward the rear. The proxy box frame is kept (identity rotation).
placement.vertical: The battery's top face touches the deck underside, which is the installed plane Z=0.
placement.longitudinal: Its rear face touches the front faces of the rear motor gearboxes (nearest clear position); the front face then ends just before the deck's oval front slot.
placement.lateral: Centred between the inner faces of the two slotted flanges.

approach.note: Nonphysical exploded start straight below the final position.

limitations: The adopted battery envelope is 38 mm wide while the photo-traced slotted-flange inner gap is 35 mm; the V40 panel shows the battery snug between the tabs, so the traced gap is slightly narrow. The resulting interference is declared and bounded to at most 2 mm depth on every face, not hidden
Hook and loop tape are zero-solid; the adhesion contact is the touching top face and carries no strength, fit or safety claim
The battery is an external tutorial envelope with no capacity, voltage or safety claim; its integral lead is a zero-solid schematic
The battery lead's HAT-end connector frame is not established, so the connect operation of this step stays BLOCKED until the Robot HAT battery connector has a source-backed frame
No installation sweep or fit is claimed
